alex: heads-up — tide24b (int4) canary is showing sporadic OOMs and high memory fragmentation on multi-turn sessions (>1024 tokens). ~2% rejected on the canary pool this morning. threw a couple of CUDA OOMs and slot-evict spikes. anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

	dana: yikes. any logs or repro prompts?

	alex: quick log snippet:```
	2026-03-22T09:12:03Z | worker-23 | AllocFailed: cudaMalloc failed (out of memory)
	KVCache: size=42MB chunks=8 free_slots=3	max_new_tokens=512	batch=8
	prefetch=on
	stack: serve->kv_prefetch->alloc_chunk
	```

	miguel: pattern looks like fragmentation vs steady-state usage. int4 reduced base mem but created more small allocations for per-token kv and attention buffers. two quick mitigations: lower default max_new_tokens from 512->256 for tide24b, and set batch.size soft cap to 4 for this model. also try kv_evict_threshold=0.6 (was 0.8).

	priya: note — we also see a small quality regression on summarization evals post-int4 quant. rouge dropped ~1.8 pts on our news dataset when using the current quant config. full eval: `/evals/run_quality.py --model tide24b --quant int4 --suite news-summ --seed 42`

	sam: +1 to Miguel's mitigations. operationally I'd rather reduce max_new_tokens and microbatch rather than revert quant immediately. but for long-context-heavy routes (chat streaming) we should fallback to int8. we can route by policy: if request.tokens_estimate > 1024 -> route to tide24b-int8.

	ci-bot: deploy canary 2026-03-22T08:50 -> tide24b-int4 v2026.03.22.08 started on pool-canary-3 (sha: a1b2c3).

	dana: I'll repro locally with the exact prompt pattern that triggered the OOM (multi-turn sys+user with long examples). running:```bash
	python tools/repro_oom.py --model tide24b --quant int4 --prompt tests/long_dialog.json --batch 8 --max_new_tokens 512
	```

	priya: I'll run the full quality sweep across our eval suites with both int4 and int8 and diff the outputs. adding `--compare-baseline=fp16` to the command to gather metrics.

	miguel: also try enabling slot_compactor experimental flag on a canary worker to reduce small-frag allocations: `slot_compactor=on, compaction_interval=60s`. if that reduces free_slots churn we can roll it to more canaries.

	alex: plan: (1) dana to repro and post heap/alloc traces (eta 2h), (2) priya to run quality sweep (eta 3h), (3) miguel to patch canary config: max_new_tokens=256, batch.soft_cap=4, kv_evict_threshold=0.6, and spin up 2 workers with slot_compactor=on (eta 1h). if quality deltas >2 pts we fallback for chat routes to int8. I'll coordinate rollback if anything gets worse. @dana @miguel @priya please update this thread with results. :thumbsup:

	dana: on it, starting repro now. I'll post `tracemalloc` / nvprof output when done.

	priya: kicked off sweeps, will drop artifacts to gs://redwood-evals/tide24b/ and ping when finished.

	miguel: deploying patched config to canary-5 and canary-6 now. toggling slot_compactor on one and leaving other as control. will report memory histograms after 30min.

	alex: thanks team — if anyone sees sudden uptick in 5xxs or latencies >2s, @alerts will page. otherwise we'll reconvene after the sweeps.
